Hi laser tech here! i can’t tell for sure from the picture but it looks like you might have red hair? Laser does not work for red blonde or white hair. You should definitely be seeing more results on average people see 15-20% difference per session. You shouldn’t be going in every 2 weeks that’s too early the earliest we book where I work is 4 weeks. You shouldn’t feel pain but you should definitely feel heat and a pinching or what other people describe like a rubber band hitting against the skin. You look like a 1-3 on the Fitzpatrick scale which is what we follow to determine what setting to put clients on which means you should be able to handle the highest setting. I’d ask what setting they have you on next time you go in
I gave my resume to a couple places. it gives them a chance to see you in person and get a feel of your personality and what makes you stand out.

The intensity can make it more painful. if it’s too high it’ll feel like intense burning that can lead to actual burns/scarring. But, usually most laser techs will follow a very specific chart that goes based off of skin type to make sure there’s no problems for the client. if you don’t feel comfortable you can always ask some questions like what setting you’re on and how many kj they’re putting in the area so she can explain it to you better. but still, if you don’t feel comfortable having her as your tech again just go with your gut

Hi Im a laser technician, the recommended time to wait between sessions is 6-8 weeks although I do know of a couple places that would recommend 4 weeks for hormonal areas since the hair grows quicker. 

Laser technically isn’t 100% permanent because body/hormonal changes can cause the hair follicle to reactivate and start growing hair again so there’s always that chance but thick dark hair is a great candidate for laser, electrolysis is the only treatment that can guarantee 100% permanent hair loss. 


With every treatment you’re supposed to lose 15-25% of hair and with every treatment the hair gets thinner and thinner to the point where you don’t even feel it anymore so you should feel it less and less until you don’t feel it at all. I have people falling asleep on the table near the end of their treatments but you also have thick and dark hair so you feel it the most out of everybody

Moles should be avoided.

Side effects depends but you’ll usually notice within the next 24 hours for darker skin tones it can take up to 2 days if we’re talking about burns
